goal: Refactor the Guix release build to move the Linux cross-toolchain definitions into a separate module.
Enables future build changes like static-PIE binaries and a stripped-down libstdc++.
reviewability: Ready to review, small self-contained refactor with no logic changes claimed.
agreement: Concept approval without stated reasons (hebasto). No objections raised.

categories.name: build
why: P2 because it is a prerequisite for static release builds (#25573) and smaller binaries (#36193), both concrete follow-on projects the author cites.
Pure reorganization with no behavior change itself, so its value is entirely as an enabler.

categories.name: tools
why: Unranked because this only touches Guix build scripts, which are covered under the build category, not general command-line tooling.

result.summary: This PR splits the Linux cross-toolchain definitions out of contrib/guix/manifest_build.scm into a new standalone Guile module, contrib/guix/toolchains.scm, and wires it up via GUIX_PACKAGE_PATH and a new linux_static.scm manifest used specifically for the Linux build phase. It is a pure reorganization: the toolchain-building code (base-binutils, make-cross-toolchain, make-bitcoin-cross-toolchain, glibc-2.31, mingw toolchain helpers) is moved essentially unchanged into a module with explicit exports, and guix-build is updated to expose that module path and use a separate manifest for the Linux static toolchain shell.
result.problem: The Guix release build's Linux and Windows toolchain definitions were entangled in one large manifest file, making it hard to reuse or vary the toolchain independently (e.g., building a static-PIE bitcoind or a stripped libstdc++) without touching unrelated manifest logic. Release engineers and contributors working on cross-toolchain changes feel this friction directly.

result.card: This PR splits the Linux cross-toolchain package definitions out of Guix's manifest_build.scm into a new toolchains.scm module, and adds a linux_static.scm manifest wired in via GUIX_PACKAGE_PATH, with no stated behavior change to the resulting binaries. The author (a maintainer) states it is 'a prerequisite for static builds (#25573)' and also enables #36193's stripped-down libstdc++ work, giving it clear leverage for upcoming release-engineering goals even though it has no direct user-facing effect itself. Only one reviewer, hebasto, has weighed in with an unelaborated Concept ACK, and no objections exist. The change is a same-day, self-contained refactor with CI passing and no rebase needed, so it is ready for review now. No PRs are noted as blocking this one, though it is itself a stated dependency for #25573 and #36193.
